 Hon'Ble Mr. Justicejaved Iqbal Wani, Judge
 Order

The instant appeals filed under and in terms of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act of 1988 arise out of a common vehicular accident caused by a vehicle bearing registration no. JK05D-4476, as such, are being decided hereunder by this common order/judgment.

1. In the instant appeal, the appellant herein has challenged the award dated 30th April, 2021, (for short "the impugned award") passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sopore (for short "the Tribunal") in claim petition titled "Naseema Begum & ors Vs. Mansoor Ahmed Mir & Ors".
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the instant appeal would reveal that the respondents 1 to 4 herein filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under and in terms of the provisions of the Act of 1988 on 27th August, 2016, claiming compensation therein on account of death of one Barkat Ahmad Dar, the husband of respondent 1 and the father of Manager National Insurance vs Naseema Begum And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182712861/
1 1|Page Mac App 41/2021 c/w Mac App 42/2021 respondents 2 to 4 herein, claimed to have been caused by a Motor Vehicle bearing Registration No. JK05D-4476 owned by the respondent 6 herein and driven by respondent 5 herein, while impleading said driver and owner as respondent therein impleaded the appellant herein also respondent in the claim petition owing to the fact that the offending vehicle was insured with it stating therein that the deceased was working as daily wager in PHE Department of the age of 43 years drawing an monthly income of Rs. 4500/- and that the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 herein were dependants on his earnings for sustenance and education.
3. The Tribunal after entertaining the claim petition issued notice to the respondents therein including the appellant herein, in response to which notice, initially none of the respondents appeared on 28th December, 2016 the date fixed yet on 27th March 2017, one Mr. Bashir Ahmad Malla, Advocate appeared on behalf of the Insurance Company appellant herein and sought time to file response to the claim petition,
however, did not file the same and instead remained absent alongwith the other respondents, resulting into setting the respondents in ex-parte on 30th June, 2017,
however, on 1st August, 2017, the counsel for the Insurance Company-appellant herein filed an application for setting aside the ex-parte proceedings which came to be set aside on 1st August, 2017 itself and written statement/response thereto also came to be filed by the counsel for the Insurance Company/appellant herein,
opposing the claim petition on multiple grounds and thereafter on the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the following issues:-
1.

sentences.text:
"Whether on 27.08.2016 the respondent-1 while driving the offending vehicle bearing registration No. JK05D-4476 2|Page Mac App 41/2021 c/w Mac App 42/2021 rashly and negligently hit Bashir Ahmad Lone, who sustained grievous injuries besides multiple fractures, was taken to SDH Sopore, however succumbed to the injuries as a result of the accident?(OPP)
2. Whether the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without holding valid driving license and other requisite documents, as such, the respondents 1 & 2 have committed the breach of policy terms and conditions and as such the respondent insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent owner?
In case issue No. 1 is proved in affirmative, to what extent and from whom the petitioners are entitled to receive
compensation?(OPP)

4. Relief"
4. The claimants in order to prove issues (1) & (3) produced five witnesses besides the claimant/respondent 1 herein appearing as a own witness in order to prove the said Manager National Insurance vs Naseema Begum And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182712861/
2 issues, whereas, the respondents including the appellant herein did not produce any witness in rebuttal thereto, whereafter the Tribunal after evaluating the evidence on record in as much as having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case in terms of the impugned award granting an amount of compensation of Rs.
10,82,000/- to the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 herein alongwith pendetelite and future interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the institution of the claim petition till its final realization, while saddling the Insurance Company/appellant herein with liability to pay said compensation to the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 herein on account of it holding that the offending vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company/appellant herein rendering it liable to indemnify the insured, the owner of the offending vehicle.
5.

As has been noticed in the preceding paras, indisputably, the Insurance Company/appellant herein though had filed response to the claim petition, yet had failed to lead any evidence in rebuttal to the evidence led by the claimants/respondents 1 to 4, so much so, also did not discharge onus to prove issue no. 3 supra, in that, onus to prove the said issue have had been put on it in view of the case set up by it against the claim petition in the response filed thereto.

7. Perusal of the record in general and the impugned award in particular would tend to show that the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 herein have discharged the onus put on them qua the issues (1) &
(3) having proved the fact of the deceased having died in the accident in question caused by the offending vehicle as also the deceased having been working as a casual laborer in the PHE Department for the last 14 years besides having earning Rs. 6,000/- per month.

Further perusal of the record available on the file would reveal that the claimants/respondents 1 to 4 herein have also proved the fact that the vehicular accident came to be caused by the offending vehicle having driven rashly and negligently by the driver of the offending vehicle respondent 5 herein as also that the vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company/appellant herein and in furtherance of the discharge of the onus, had also placed on record documentary evidence in the shape of the copy of FIR No. 353/2016 of Police Station, Sopore, registered in respect of the accident in question as also the death certificate of the deceased besides the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle as also the insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle covering the insurance on the date of accident.

sentences.text: The standard of proof in such like matters is one of preponderance of probabilities, rather than beyond reasonable doubt.

One needs to be mindful that the approach and role of Courts while examining evidence in accident claim cases ought not to be to find fault with non-examination of some best eyewitnesses, as may happen in a criminal trial; but, instead should be only to analyze the material placed on record by the parties to ascertain whether the claimant's version is more likely than not true."
9.
